A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAT benchmark and tracking method despite the changed title and method name. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAT simulation experiments comparing R-VAT with AOT and D-VAT, plus curriculum, randomization and reward ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds disturbance tests, real-video action evaluations and reported physical-drone tracking results.

M1.justification: GC-VAT retains R-VAT's CNN-GRU architecture, PPO objectives, normalized goal-centered reward, two-stage curriculum and randomization ranges. Renaming, new pseudocode and expanded benchmark-tool descriptions do not establish a changed tracking procedure.

E1.justification: The original six scenes and four weather conditions remain. v2 additionally evaluates wind disturbances, synthetic rain, similar-looking distractors and an unseen bus target, plus eight videos each from VOT, DTB70 and UAVDT and physical DJI drone tracking. These substantially extend evaluated environments and transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds a random-action policy to the real-video comparisons in Table 7 and Tables 18–20. AOT and D-VAT remain the evaluated DAT baselines, with their existing reproduction adaptations retained in Appendix D.

E3.justification: Existing DAT training budgets, CR/TSR metrics and 40-episode evaluation remain. New protocols introduce framewise Correct Action Rate on recorded videos, physical-drone evaluation, wind perturbations of 2.5–7.5 m/s and yaw disturbances of 0.05–0.15 rad/s. Synthetic-rain testing excludes snowy conditions from cross-domain evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds robustness analyses testing wind, precipitation, distractor confusion and transfer to an unseen target class (Tables 5–6), alongside real-video action case studies. The original curriculum, randomization and reward ablations remain; their consolidation into Table 4 is not a removal.

E5.justification: Section 5.4 newly reports a t-test with p < 0.001 for real-video action performance versus the random policy. Existing DAT reporting of means and variance over 40 evaluation episodes is retained; neither version establishes an increased training-seed count.

E6.justification: New results include CAR values of 0.795, 0.833 and 0.802 on VOT, DTB70 and UAVDT, plus physical-drone TSR of 88.4% and CAR of 81.3%. Robustness scores and per-video results are also added. Original detailed DAT Tables 12–17 are numerically unchanged, although some main-text summaries are revised, including farmland cross-domain TSR from 0.66 to 0.65.

T1.justification: v1 already contains substantial reward-failure proofs in Appendix C.1. v2 replaces the D-VAT-specific directional and camera-frustum derivations with an explicit reward-monotonicity principle, Proposition 1, Remark 1 and a different projection-based counterexample proof. This substantially revises the mathematical argument, while retaining the normalized deviation underlying the reward.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, goal-centered reward and curriculum contributions remain. v2 adds explicit novelty claims concerning the first open-world air-to-ground benchmark and unlimited scene generation, and extends claimed validation to real imagery. The abstract replaces the approximately 400% cumulative-reward improvement headline with approximately 72% simulator tracking success.

C2.justification: New Appendix F qualifies deployment evidence as covering real images and simple physical scenarios, identifying similar distractors and the simulation–reality gap as remaining barriers. v2 also explains the high drone speed as discouraging a trivial single-action policy and interprets low baseline variance as failed learning. Earlier scene-specific and snow-related limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds curriculum pseudocode, osm_importer processing and file-format details, an explicit training-versus-testing privileged-information distinction, and DJI deployment hardware, SDK and communication details. It replaces the project-page pointer with an explicit benchmark/code repository link. Existing architecture, PPO hyperparameters and simulation budgets remain documented.

R1.justification: The related-work survey is largely retained. The introduction and Table 1 sharpen comparisons around full dynamics, human-like target behavior and digital-twin scene construction. Added citations include AirSim, foundation-model/offline-RL tracking, real-video benchmarks and rain restoration; these citations do not represent additional evaluated DAT baselines.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and method exposition, changes the title and method name, places reward design before curriculum training, and introduces dedicated theory and real-world experiment sections. It also reorganizes the appendices and adds contents, limitations and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. v2 redraws the overview, combines scene illustrations with benchmark statistics, adds reward-contour and real-world deployment displays, consolidates main-text ablation tables, and replaces the earlier proof diagrams. New robustness and real-video tables and figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's simulation-only evaluation, v2 provides useful robustness tests and initial real-video and physical-drone evidence, while Appendix F makes remaining deployment limitations explicit. The gain is constrained by a random-policy-only real-video comparison and sparse CAR scoring and physical-drone trial details. The additions strengthen feasibility evidence, but leave broad open-world reliability unresolved.
